title: That Woman from the Market
description:
A neighborhood alley. Passing a small banchan shop when a voice called out.

"Hey? Aren't you that young man from before?"

The woman who'd held out her card at the convenience-store register.

"This is my shop. So you live around here too."

choices.text: "Thank you for that day. Really." — bow properly
choices.result_text:
She waved it off.
"Oh, that was nothing. Buy some side dishes, I'll give you a discount."

Bought rolled omelette and stir-fried anchovies. She charged half.

Started dropping by once a week after that.
On the third container, 'Kim Minjun' was written across the lid in black marker.

choices.text: Too awkward — just nod and walk past
choices.result_text:
Lowered his head and walked faster.

She said something else from behind. Pretended not to hear.

Before turning the corner, {name} looked back once. She was handing another customer a bag, and the shop's glass door was slowly closing.

title: A Face That Remembers
description:
In front of a banchan shop in a neighborhood alley.

"Young man. The convenience store, right?"

The woman whose card he'd refused at the register.

"You wouldn't take it, to the end. Rare these days, that."

She held out a container of side dishes. "This one's free. Refuse and I'll get angry."

choices.text: Accept it this time
choices.result_text:
Took the container. Rolled omelette.

"See? Feels good to receive, doesn't it."

Back at the goshiwon, ate it over rice.
Tried to calculate how long it had been since he'd eaten someone's home cooking.
The calculation failed.

Next week, took the empty container back to the shop. That was the beginning.

choices.text: "The thought is enough" — decline again
choices.result_text:
She sighed.
"All right. Just make sure you eat."

She put the container back in the refrigerated display.

At the goshiwon, {name} peeled open a bowl of instant rice. One side of the little table was still empty where the banchan could have gone.

title: The Banchan Shop's Son
description:
Stopped by the shop — an unfamiliar man was there.

Early 40s. Suit. Helping with his mother's shop.

"Ah, you're the one Mother talked about. The convenience store."

He pulled out a business card. HR team lead at a mid-sized company.

"My mother's eye for people is accurate. Thirty years of running a shop."

choices.text: Find the courage — "Are there any open positions?"
choices.result_text:
The man smiled.
"Send your resume. With Mother's recommendation, your documents get read. Guaranteed."

Sent the resume that week. The interview call came.

Below the interview date on the phone, the banchan shop's number was now saved under 'Owner.'

choices.text: Don't want to impose — just take the card
choices.result_text:
"Thank you," and put the card in the wallet.

The woman packed the anchovies and said, "Call if you change your mind."

Back at the goshiwon, the corner of the card stuck out over the transit card. {name} did not save the number.

title: Replying to the Invitation
description:
Eight weeks after handing in the wallet, a text arrived from an unsaved number.

"Thank you for the other day. Can I buy you a meal?"

The reply field beneath the message was still empty. The sender had made an invitation, nothing more. No date or place had been set.

choices.text: Accept — send an available Saturday afternoon first
choices.result_text:
{name} typed an available time into the reply field first.
"Thank you. This Saturday afternoon works for me."

A new message arrived a moment later.
"Then let's meet at ○○ Korean Restaurant in Gangnam, Saturday at 12:30."

{name} sent the date and address back for confirmation.
"Yes, see you then."
Only after both sides confirmed did he add it to his calendar.

choices.text: Decline the meal — reply with thanks only
choices.result_text:
{name} sent a short reply.
"I appreciate the thought. I'm just glad the wallet made it back to you."

He did not ask for a date or place beneath the send time. Nothing went on the calendar. No meeting was arranged.

title: Lunch with the Executive
description:
Saturday, 12:30. The Korean restaurant in Gangnam they had both confirmed.

The wallet's owner — the executive — was already there.

"That wallet had my mother's photo in it. Her last one."

He paused for a moment.

"A meal doesn't repay it. But first, I was curious what kind of person you are."

choices.text: Tell him everything. Including the current situation
choices.result_text:
Six years spent paying down debt, the place he lived now, the plan through age thirty-eight.
Said it all. No packaging.

The executive put down his spoon and listened.

"Someone who pays off debt for six years and starts again — that's rare even inside a company."

At parting, he said:
"I'll look into a position at an affiliate. Not a favor. You pass the verification yourself."

choices.text: Deflect politely. Don't want to show everything
choices.result_text:
"I'm preparing various things."

He didn't press. The food was good.

At parting, he gave a business card.
"Call if you need anything."

{name} put the card deep inside his wallet. He never saved the executive's number.

title: Verification
description:
The affiliate company the executive mentioned called.

Documents passed. Interview scheduled.

Sitting in the interview room, one of the interviewers looked up from the file.

"Your referral path is unusual. What's your relationship with the executive director?"

The air in the room shifted.

choices.text: Tell the wallet story exactly as it happened
choices.result_text:
"I found his wallet at a subway station and returned it. That's all."

The interviewers looked at each other. One smiled.
"We heard that story. We wanted to hear it from you."

The offer came three days later. Base pay was 4.55 million won a month.

On the first morning, {name} rubbed a thumb over the affiliate logo on his new employee badge.

choices.text: Just say "It's a personal connection"
choices.result_text:
The interviewer nodded. Didn't ask further.

The result was rejection.

Later, a text from the executive:
'Why didn't you tell the wallet story? That's your best credential.'

{name} wrote a reply, then erased it. Only the rejection email's subject line remained on the screen.

title: The Envelope's Owner
description:
Night shift. The door opened.

That customer. The one who'd retrieved the envelope.

"We meet again. Thank you for that, truly."

He put a box of drinks on the counter.
"This isn't for the owner — it's for you. And — are you free on weekends? I do interior work, and we're short-handed. Daily pay."

choices.text: Take the weekend site job
choices.result_text:
Saturday dawn, a villa site in Hwagok-dong.

Wallpaper assist, hauling materials, cleanup. The body ached.

The boss taught constantly while working. Material costs, how to write estimates, how to deal with building owners.

130,000 won for the day. But what was learned over his shoulder was worth more.
"Coming next week too?" the boss asked.

choices.text: "The thought is enough" — politely decline
choices.result_text:
"I have my shift. Thank you though."

He nodded and left a business card.

Hid the drink box from the owner and drank one can per night shift.

Around the last can, the business card came to mind.
Couldn't remember where it went.

title: The Boss's Offer
description:
Another weekend on site.

During teardown, the boss sat down next to {name}.

"Starting next month I'm running two sites at once. I need someone to organize estimates and move between them."

"Come in as office staff. Base pay is 2.24 million won a month. Learn the sites and I'll raise it."

"I saw that you're honest. In this business, that's the rarest thing there is."

choices.text: Accept. Learn on site.
choices.result_text:
A 500,000-won site handover allowance came first. Base pay would be 2.24 million won a month from then on.

{name} tucked the estimate binder under one arm and walked through the empty site.

On the first attendance sheet linking the desk and the job site, he wrote his own name.

choices.text: Decline. My path is elsewhere.
choices.result_text:
"I'm grateful, but I have a direction I'm heading."

The boss looked disappointed but smiled.
"Fine. But remember. There's always a seat for you."

During teardown, {name} put the boss's worn tape measure on top of the toolbox. That night, he left the site's group chat.

title: The Paper on the Wall
description:
Walking to the convenience store shift. An A4 sheet taped to the glass door.

'Has anyone seen a black envelope last week?
It's my mother's surgery money. Reward offered.
Contact: 010-XXXX-XXXX'

{name} stood in front of it for a long time.

That envelope is in the goshiwon drawer right now.

choices.text: Call and return it. Refuse the reward.
choices.result_text:
"I have it. I'm sorry. I'll bring it right away."

The man came running. Taking the envelope, he bowed.
"Thank you. Thank you so much."

He offered the reward. Couldn't take it. Hadn't earned the right.

Walking home, the body felt light.
First deep sleep in a week.

choices.text: Pretend not to see it. Too late now.
choices.result_text:
Walked past the paper to the shift.

A week later it fell off, soaked in rain.

The 500,000 won was still in the drawer. It had not been spent.

One dawn after work, the envelope caught on the frame when {name} tried to close the drawer. The handle would not shut on the first try.

title: Moving Day
description:
Saturday morning. The hallway was loud.

Next door — the one who passed the exam — was packing out.

Three boxes, one suitcase, one blanket. Six months of living, in total.

"Oh, {name}. I'm leaving today."

On the stairs, a box wobbled.

choices.text: Help carry the boxes
choices.result_text:
Carried boxes together. Three trips to the truck.

After loading, they came back with two canned coffees.

"You're the first person I got attached to in a goshiwon."

Exchanged numbers. The truck pulled out of the alley.

The light next door would not come on again. The new contact remained on {name}'s phone.

choices.text: Just say "good luck out there"
choices.result_text:
"You worked hard. Live well."

They smiled and carried the boxes down.

That evening, the door next door stood open. An exam-document envelope lay discarded on the floor.

Only then did {name} realize he had never asked the neighbor's name.

title: A Text from the District Office
description:
A text arrived. The former neighbor.

'{name}, I got posted to ○○ District Office.
And — a youth housing support program just opened.
I think you qualify. Apply before the deadline, please.
Sending the notice link. This is public info, so no pressure.'

choices.text: Apply immediately
choices.result_text:
Gathered the documents and applied. Selected.

Six months of rent support. 1.2 million won total.

{name} sent a screenshot of the approval message.
'I applied because of you. Thank you.'

A thumbs-up emoji arrived a moment later.

choices.text: Save the link and plan to apply over the weekend
choices.result_text:
The weekend passed. When {name} opened the notice the next day, 'Applications Closed' was stamped across the page.

He drafted a reply.
'Thank you for telling me. I missed it.'

His finger stayed over the send button for a long time.

title: Regular
description:
2:30 AM. The door opened.

The man with the low-pulled cap. Again.

Two triangle sandwiches, one energy drink. Same combination.

"This place is the most comfortable. Nobody acts like they know me."

He hesitated at the register.
"Last time, you pretended not to recognize me — I know. Thank you for that."

choices.text: "At this hour, everyone here is just a person"
choices.result_text:
The man smiled. Not the screen smile — just a tired person's smile.

Days later, his voice came on the radio.
"There's this convenience store I go to. The person working there treats me like just a person. In Seoul at dawn, you have no idea how big that is."

He didn't say which store.
Only {name} knew. That was enough.

choices.text: Ask for just one photo
choices.result_text:
"Um... could I get one picture?"

The man paused, then nodded.
"Just don't post it anywhere."

Took it. Never posted it. A promise is a promise.

The man didn't come back after that. The photograph stayed in a private album.

title: Same Method
description:
Hongdae street. Evening.

A familiar back. Worn jacket, clean envelope.

The scammer. Mapo redevelopment info, 500,000 won.

Right now he was waving the envelope at some college student.
The student's expression — {name}'s expression from three months ago.

choices.text: Step in. "That man is a scammer."
choices.result_text:
The student and the scammer turned at the same time.

The scammer recognized {name}. Half a second. Then simply walked away.
Didn't even run. This wasn't his first time.

The student asked, "You know him?"
"Cost me 500,000 won to know him."

The student put the wallet back in a pocket and disappeared across the crosswalk.

choices.text: Walk past. Not my business.
choices.result_text:
Didn't slow down.

At the end of the block, {name} looked back once. The student was taking out a wallet.

Even after the lights were off that night, the hand shaking the document envelope and the open wallet kept alternating in his mind. He turned the phone face down.
